newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields were largely unchanged on Tuesday in thin trade. The crown was just about unchanged against the mark, but weaker against the dollar and sterling.
"Trading volumes were very low. Therefore it is not surprising the market has not moved very much," one trader said.

The spread between Swedish and German ten-year bonds decreased by one basis point to 92 basis points. In the early session the spread was at 90 basis points, partly due to a small recoil from yesterday. Italian debt markets also gave some support, according to dealers.

The Swedish crown was somewhat weaker against the trade weighted TCW-index, to 122.24 from 121.67 from late Monday. The main reasons are the generally stronger dollar and sterling, according to traders. The crown was just about unchanged against the mark at 4.4195 from 4.4170 yesterday.

The next domestic focus will be a forecast on the PSBR from the Swedish National Debt Office Wednesday at 0730 gmt. The results of an auction of T-bills of a total of 10 billion crowns will be released tomorrow at 1050 gmt.
